summary: This PR adds a single new documentation/patch-record file (ai-os/patches/quality-gate-node-oom-memory-cap-2026-07-26.diff) recording a live fix already applied to the shared, out-of-repo /opt/veridian/scripts/quality-gate.sh, per this repo's established convention (verified against 18 other existing ai-os/patches/*.diff files following the same pattern). I independently verified the claim is not a self-report stub: the live script at /opt/veridian/scripts/quality-gate.sh actually contains the exact NODE_OPTIONS export described, placed correctly inside the `if [ -f package.json ]` block before lint/build/test run, with proper preservation of any pre-existing NODE_OPTIONS via `${NODE_OPTIONS:-}` rather than clobbering it, and exported so child npm/pnpm/bun processes inherit it. The fix is a sound, low-risk mitigation matching Next.js's own documented guidance for constrained-memory build environments, correctly diagnosed via journalctl evidence (OOM-killer, not an AI logic stall) cited in the commit message. The diff itself touches no application code, no .github/workflows/**, no auth/payment/billing/rls/migration paths, and introduces no secrets or security issues -- it is purely additive documentation, consistent with tier1 classification.
